content:
Garage door screen sliders stand as a commendable solution for homeowners seeking to relish the invigorating outdoors while maintaining a barrier against pesky insects. Despite the convenience they offer, these systems are not impervious to common issues that may impede their seamless operation. This comprehensive guide aims to delve into the typical challenges associated with garage door screen sliders, offering practical solutions to ensure that your setup remains functional and free from unnecessary hassles.

Throughout this guide, we will navigate through the nuances of these common issues of garage door screen sliders. From difficulties in sliding the screen and issues with latches to concerns about torn or damaged screens, each problem will be met with effective remedies. As we explore solutions, the focus will be on practical measures that homeowners can implement to troubleshoot and maintain the optimal performance of their garage door screen sliders.

By understanding and proactively addressing these challenges, homeowners can ensure that their garage door screen sliders continue to serve as a reliable and effective barrier against insects while providing a refreshing outdoor experience. Embracing these practical solutions enhances the longevity of the system, contributing to a hassle-free and enjoyable living environment.

1. Difficulty Sliding: Dealing with Track Obstructions

One of the most prevalent issues is difficulty in sliding the screen open or closed. Over time, dirt, debris, or rust can accumulate in the tracks, hindering the smooth movement of the screen. To address this, it’s essential to regularly clean the tracks using a soft brush or vacuum to remove any debris. Additionally, lubricate the tracks with a silicone-based spray to facilitate effortless sliding.

2. Screen Won’t Stay in Place: Tackling Latch and Tension Problems

If the screen on your device does not remain in the appropriate position, this might be an indication of a latch that is not operating properly or tension-related difficulties. The latch should be inspected for any signs of damage, and if it is found to be damaged, it should be replaced. In order to fix the problem, you need to adjust the tension on the screen by either tightening or loosening the screws that are located on the sides.

3. Torn or Damaged Screens: Maintaining Optimal Visibility

It is possible for screens to experience wear and tear, which can result in rips or defects that significantly reduce their efficiency. The usage of a screen repair kit allows for the repairing of minor rips in the screen. On the other hand, if the damage is significant, you might want to think about replacing the entire screen. You will be able to fix any screen faults more quickly if you do regular inspections.

4. Rolling Up Unevenly: Ensuring Smooth Operations

In the event that the screen rolls up in an uneven manner, it may be an indication that there are issues with the roller mechanism or irregular tension. In order to fix this issue, you should first check the rollers for any blockages and then carefully clean them. You should adjust the tension on both sides in order to get a roll-up that is smooth and even.

5. Sagging Screen: Reinforcing Structural Integrity

Sagging screens not only affect functionality but also impact the overall aesthetics. Check for loose or damaged frame components and tighten screws or replace damaged parts as needed. For persistent sagging, consider adding additional support to the frame.

6. Stuck or Jammed: Eliminating Obstructions

Screens are susceptible to being caught or jammed on occasion as a result of clutter or misalignment. Conduct a comprehensive search of the tracks for any foreign items and remove them if you find any. In order to avoid repeat jams, it is important to ensure that the tracks are properly aligned and to lubricate any moving parts.

7. Frame Damage: Addressing Structural Issues

Frames may suffer damage over time, affecting the entire functionality of the screen. Assess the extent of the damage and repair minor issues with patches or epoxy. For severe damage, replacing the entire frame may be the most effective solution.

8. Motorized Screen Not Responding: Electrical Troubleshooting

It is possible for motorized garage door screen sliders to experience problems such as inability to respond or movements that are not consistent. To get started, you should examine the power supply, replace the batteries, or investigate any electrical issues that may be present. For more precise instructions on motorized systems, please see the handbook provided by the manufacturer.

9. Weather Stripping Wear and Tear: Ensuring Proper Insulation

There is a correlation between worn weather stripping and decreased insulation as well as increased insect ingress. Maintaining an effective barrier against pests and the elements of the outdoors requires that weather stripping be inspected and replaced on a regular basis.

10. Insect Infestation: Enhancing Protective Measures

Despite having a garage door screen, insects may find their way inside. Regularly inspect the screen for gaps, holes, or damaged areas. Repair or replace the screen as needed and consider using insect repellents or traps in the vicinity to prevent infestations.

content:
Planning on a screening project involves critical decisions, with the choice of screen mesh playing a pivotal role. Prioritizing between visibility and durability, selecting a color finish that complements your home, and addressing specific needs like solar protection or allergy filters are essential considerations.

For properties frequently troubled by insects, determining the required level of protection becomes paramount. While standard fiberglass screening may suffice, situations demanding heightened defense often call for specific types of tiny mesh screens, colloquially known as no-see-um screens.

Whether you’re focused on insect protection, solar shielding, or allergy prevention, delving into the nuances of tiny mesh screens empowers you to make informed decisions tailored to your home project’s unique requirements.

By striking the right balance between visibility, durability, and specialized functionalities, you can ensure that your screening project not only meets its goals but also enhances the overall functionality and aesthetics of your property.

What is a no-see-um screen?

While our screens offer insect protection, there are certain types of bugs, colloquially known as “no-see-ums,” that are small enough to penetrate them. It’s essential to note that “no-see-ums” specifically refer to tiny, blood-sucking, biting flies. Additionally, other minuscule insects like gnats and sandflies can pose a similar challenge. Coastal homes, in particular, are prone to issues with these insects, making them the most likely to benefit from screens designed specifically for no-see-ums. 

The term encompasses a range of tiny pests, and even though the common name implies invisibility, they can still pose a nuisance. Employing screens tailored to combat these tiny invaders is crucial for ensuring comprehensive protection, especially in regions where these pests are prevalent, allowing homeowners to enjoy their living spaces without the intrusion of these bothersome insects. 

Types of No-See-Um Screen

We have several different options for those in need of no-see-um screening: 

  • No-See-Um 20×20 Fiberglass Mesh

This is our standard no-see-um screening. It is more durable than regular fiberglass screen, but less so than some of the following options. It is extremely versatile and can be used anywhere you would put a window screen. 

  • 24×22 Aluminum Tiny Mesh

An even tighter mesh, this will protect against almost any insect as well as prevent a good amount of dirt and debris from entering your space. The aluminum material makes this a great economy option. This mesh material also provides excellent visibility and airflow!

  • 20×30 Solar Insect Screen

On top of protecting from even the tiniest pests, our solar insect screen also protects against 65% of UV exposure. Use it to protect your skin from the sun’s harmful rays and reduce your home’s A/C costs. 

  • 20×17 Super Screen Tiny Mesh

For places in your home where you want extra durability, Super Screen tiny mesh has you covered. Made from vinyl-coated polyester, this heavy-duty screen can stand up to the elements, time, and of course, tiny insects. 

  • 20×20 Super Screen No-See-Um Mesh

The strongest no-see-um protection on the market. Keep even the smallest insects out of your home, porch, or pool enclosure for years to come with a 20×20 Super Screen. 

No-see-um screen vs regular (fiberglass) screen

So, is a no-see-um screen a better choice than standard fiberglass for your next project? If most likely depends on what level of protection you require. Both screens can be used for windows, pool cages, patios, and screen doors, and both offer some level of insect protection. For a better idea of your options, breaking down the pros and cons of each mesh is always a good first step. 

Fiberglass Screen Pros and Cons

Fiberglass screen mesh is the most commonly used screening available, as it’s flexible and inexpensive. 

Fiberglass Screen: Pros

  • Insect protection against larger bugs
  • Economy option
  • Easy to install

Fiberglass Screen: Cons

  • Standard durability
  • Only protects against larger insects

No-See-Um Screen Pros and Cons

If your home attracts no-see-ums, sand flies, or gnats, consider no-see-um mesh. Ideal for coastal areas, it thwarts these tiny insects, making it a popular choice for comprehensive protection. 

No-See-Um Screen: Pros

  • Increased durability (even more so for tiny mesh Super Screen)
  • Longer lasting
  • Protection against even the smallest pests

  • Increased daytime privacy

No-See-Um Screen: Cons

title: Do I Need a Permit to Rescreen a Pool Cage?
excerpt: Undertaking rescreening a pool cage is a practical and transformative home upgrade that adds value to outdoor spaces while safeguarding against pesky insects.
content:
Undertaking rescreening a pool cage is a practical and transformative home upgrade that adds value to outdoor spaces while safeguarding against pesky insects. This improvement, however, prompts a crucial inquiry: Do I need a permit to rescreen a pool cage?

Before diving into the rescreening project, homeowners must navigate the intricate regulatory landscape governing construction and alterations. The necessity of a permit often hinges on local building codes and the scope of the planned modifications. While a straightforward rescreening—limited to replacing the mesh material—might be classified as maintenance, structural changes or alterations to the existing framework could trigger permit requirements.

Understanding these nuances is essential to ensure compliance with local regulations. By clarifying the need for a permit upfront, homeowners can streamline the planning process, avoiding potential legal complications and ensuring a smooth and hassle-free rescreening journey.

Understanding the Basics

Rescreening a pool cage may or may not require a permit in many areas, depending on the nature of the alterations and local building requirements. Permits are usually needed for projects involving structural modifications or revisions to the current structure. Simple rescreening, on the other hand, may be classified as maintenance as opposed to building because it only requires changing the mesh material.

Local Building Codes

Local building codes serve as the foundation for permit requirements. These codes vary widely, reflecting regional considerations such as climate, wind loads, and safety standards. Before initiating a pool cage rescreening project, homeowners should contact their local building department or check online resources to understand the specific regulations in their area.

Factors Influencing Permit Requirements

  • Structural Changes: If the rescreening project involves structural changes, such as modifying the frame or altering the dimensions of the pool cage, a permit is likely required. Structural alterations are considered construction projects and fall within the jurisdiction of building codes.
  • Wind Load Considerations: Areas prone to hurricanes or strong winds often have specific requirements regarding the design and construction of pool cages. Any alterations that impact the structure’s ability to withstand wind loads might necessitate a permit.
  • Enclosure Type: Some jurisdictions differentiate between screen enclosures and solid enclosures. While rescreening a traditional screen enclosure might not trigger permit requirements, the same may not hold true for enclosures with solid roofs or walls.

Benefits of Obtaining a Permit

While navigating the permit process may seem cumbersome, securing the necessary approvals brings several advantages:

  • Legal Compliance: Obtaining a permit ensures that the rescreening project complies with local building codes and regulations, preventing potential legal issues in the future.
  • Safety Assurance: Permitted projects undergo scrutiny to meet safety standards, enhancing the overall structural integrity of the pool cage.
  • Home Value: Having permitted improvements can positively impact the resale value of a home, assuring potential buyers that the modifications meet regulatory standards.

DIY vs. Professional Rescreening

Whether homeowners choose to tackle the rescreening project themselves or hire professionals, permit requirements remain applicable. DIY enthusiasts must adhere to the same regulations as contractors, emphasizing the importance of understanding local building codes before initiating any work.

Steps to Determine Permit Requirements

  • Contact the Local Building Department: Reach out to the local building department to inquire about specific permit requirements for rescreening a pool cage in your area. They can provide information on the application process and associated fees.
  • Detailed Project Plans: If the rescreening project involves structural changes, prepare detailed plans outlining the modifications. These plans will be crucial when applying for a permit.
  • Consult a Professional: Seeking advice from a licensed contractor or structural engineer can provide valuable insights into whether the planned rescreening project requires a permit. Professionals often have experience navigating local building codes.

Conclusion

Rescreening a pool cage is a surefire way to breathe new life into outdoor spaces and enhance the overall aesthetics of a home. However, one must not overlook the critical aspect of understanding whether a permit is required for this transformative project. The intricacies of local building codes, the specific nature of the rescreening project, and considerations regarding structural changes all converge to determine permit requirements.

Proactive engagement with the permitting process is not merely a formality but a strategic move that ensures more than just legal compliance. By obtaining the necessary permits, homeowners contribute to the safety and longevity of their pool cage rescreening endeavor. The scrutiny involved in the permitting process helps guarantee that the project aligns with established standards, fostering structural integrity and adherence to safety protocols.

This thoughtful approach not only safeguards against potential legal repercussions but also reinforces the homeowner’s commitment to a well-executed and enduring pool cage enhancement, promoting a harmonious blend of aesthetics and functionality in their outdoor living spaces.

title: 5 Reasons Why You Should Install A Pet Door at Home

content:
Our lovely pets are considered a cherished part of the family for good reason. All pets bring so much joy to the household, no matter how big or small.

If you’re a pet owner and proud fur parent, you know how much your four-legged friend loves to venture out and about. Pets enjoy exploring the outdoors as much as they love following you around indoors. However, letting your pet in and out by opening and closing doors for them many times a day and through the night can become tiring and an inconvenience.

Pet doors offer pets seamless in-and-out access, enhancing convenience. Explore the benefits and key considerations of why you should install a pet door at home.

About pet doors

Pet doors can be made of vinyl, plastic, rubber, or polycarbonate material and come in all shapes and sizes (just like your pets do!). Pet doors come in many types, with loads of different features, and can be installed in either wood or glass (or both)

At American Rescreening, we install pet doors suited for glass and can safely install a pet door into your glass panel at home.

Why get a pet door?

Simply, having a pet door is a practical and convenient solution for active pets with busy owners.  Pets come with lots of responsibilities and installing one that fits your home, your pet and your circumstances can be a game changer. Here are a few benefits a pet door can offer.

Pet doors give your pets more freedom

Most pets love to run around the garden, roll around on the grass, or just bask in the sunshine. With a handy pet door installed, they can move around and get back in as they please without disturbing you. Gone are the days of leaving the door open or the constant up and down to let your furry family members in and out.

Pet doors encourage your pets to be more active

Allowing your pet to enter and leave as they please will help them stay stimulated and not get bored if they are home all day by themselves.  Whether it’s a door into their cat enclosure or a door to the backyard, having additional space for your pet to come and go can help add to the daily exercise they need and the enrichment to keep them happy.

Pet doors help with toilet training and avoiding indoor accidents

One of the major concerns for pets and homeowners is the little accidents that can happen inside the house. Unfortunately, if your pet can’t get out to the grass, indoor accidents can occur. And when they are young, this can be an arduous task of taking them out many times a day!   So, giving pets easy access to the outside allows them to relieve themselves at their (and your) convenience.

Pet doors can reduce your worry

If you’re running around with a busy schedule, you may sometimes forget that your cat or dog is still inside as you head out or they may be outside as you turn in for the night. With a pet door, they can let themselves in whenever it starts to rain or if it gets too hot outside, so they can be safe in the comfort of their home.

It’s good for the fur parent, too

Having a pet door will save you the time and frustration of having to open and close the door for your pet all day long, not to mention saving on energy costs if you have a heating or cooling system running.

What should you consider when choosing and installing a pet door?

If you’ve been thinking of a pet door for your home, but aren’t sure of what to do next, here are three important things to consider before purchasing a pet door.

The size of your pet – you need to choose a pet door that will suit your pet when they are full-grown. Make sure you take measurements of your pet (if fully grown) to check they can get through the door comfortably.

Where you want to locate the pet door – The best access for your pet to reach the outdoors is via a door, window, or panel.  The pet door should open onto an enclosed, secure area like a courtyard, cat enclosure, or backyard, and not be visible from the street or passers-by.

title: A Guide to Pet Screens, Doors, and Guards
excerpt: Pet ownership is great, but perhaps less so when they engage in destructive behaviors in the home. Issues like indoor urination or furniture scratching present substantial challenges.
content:
Pet ownership is great, but perhaps less so when they engage in destructive behaviors in the home. Issues like indoor urination or furniture scratching present substantial challenges.

Thankfully, one of those destructive behaviors can be easily addressed – the scratching and breaking of screen doors.

Pet screen doors provide ventilation, natural light, and protection from insects and small animals. At the same time, they offer advantages to pets, such as refreshing breezes and scenic views.

Also, screens contribute significantly to pet safety, confining them to designated areas, preventing interactions with other animals, reducing exposure to high-traffic zones, and minimizing the risk of getting loose. 

While pets may occasionally pose challenges, preserving the integrity of your screen doors can be a simple yet effective solution to ensuring the well-being of your furry friends as well as you’re your home.

How pets can damage doors

If a screen door is all that stands between your dog and the great outdoors, chances are the dog will scratch at it until something happens. 

And it’s not just dogs. Cats claw anything and love to scratch at things that offer resistance, like screens. Scratching by dogs and cats can rip or fray screens and damage the screen’s frame.

Because the screens are so thin and sometimes hard to see, pets may not realize they are there and go barreling into them if they see a squirrel or bird walking by. Again, this can easily rip the screen or damage the frame.

How do you prevent your pet from destroying your screens?

 There are three very effective and cost-efficient ways to prevent your screens from being damaged by your animals:

Pet-resistant screens

Probably the easiest solution is to invest in pet-resistant screens (also known as “pet-proof screens”). These heavy-duty pet-resistant screens are designed to fit in the frames you already have but are made of stronger and more durable materials that can withstand most scratching and pushing from your furry little friends. 

In addition, pet-resistant screens blend in with the rest of your decor, so the untrained eye wouldn’t even know you have a dog. Pet-resistant screens also work for windows and other enclosures like doors and pet patios.

Your pet’s size will determine the best screen for your needs. Talk to your American Rescreening technician to find the best pet screen solution for you. The three most popular pet-resistant screens are Pet Screens, Tuff Screens, and Super Screens. 

Pet guards

Pet guards are stylized metal gates that protect your door from your pet. For larger or more determined dogs, screen door pet guards offer a more robust barrier than a pet-resistant screen because they are made of metal instead of mesh. You don’t have to worry about your pet damaging the existing screen because they won’t be able to get to it physically. However, these are harder to install on sliding screens and patio doors.

Our door guards protect your screens from the claws of your four-legged friends and from people’s feet, knees, and other body parts that can potentially ruin your screen door.

Pet doors

A pet door (also known as a doggie door) can help your pet enter and exit your home, so there’s no need for scratching to get out. Traditionally, doggie doors are installed directly into a front door or as a panel for sliding doors. However, American Rescreening offers screen doors with a pre-installed pet door, or you can easily install a pet screen door in whatever door you already own.

Screen doors with pet doors are great for more independent cats and dogs. They allow them to safely come and go whenever they choose and provide excellent scratch protection. We will install the best option to suit your needs. Pet doors can be mounted inside both swinging and sliding screen doors.

What are pet-resistant screens made of?

Pet-resistant screens are usually made from PVC-coated polyester yarn, making them seven times more resilient than standard screens. The strong, pliable mesh can withstand repeated clawing by cats and dogs. Thanks to the PVC vinyl lining, the screens can hold up to the sun and other elements longer. While the mesh is thicker than a regular screen, the spaces are larger to facilitate airflow and light. But don’t worry; the holes are still small enough to keep out the bugs.

Do pet-resistant screens work?

The short answer is yes! Pet-resistant screens are tear and puncture-resistant, but if your big dog runs full force into a pet-resistant screen door, it may damage the frame. But yes, pet-resistant screens do a fantastic job of preventing expensive replacements and repairs.

How do you pet-proof a window screen?

Using a pet-resistant screen is the best approach to pet-proof your window screen. If your dog or cat has a favorite window, you might pet-proof it with a scratch-resistant material while using regular screens for the rest of your windows. While you could use a screen guard, you might not like how it looks. It is also not advised to install a pet door in a window, particularly one not on the first floor.

title: A Definitive Guide To Pool Rescreening

content:
If you’ve owned your pool for a while, it might be time to replace the enclosing screen. Screens, whether their nominal lifespans are five or ten years, will deteriorate over time. A deteriorating screen will no longer provide the same level of protection and comfort and detract from the overall pool experience.

Replacing the screen yourself is difficult – rescreening should be left to the pros. Here’s a definitive guide to pool rescreening to help you understand why you should hire only the best company like us.

When should you rescreen your pool?

You should rescreen your pool enclosure when you notice signs of wear and tear or damage to the existing screen. Regular inspections and maintenance are key to ensuring the longevity and functionality of your pool screen enclosure. Here are some guidelines:

  • Annual inspection: Perform a thorough inspection at least once a year. Look for tears, holes, or loose sections. Check the frame for rust or corrosion.
  • Storm damage: After severe storms or hurricanes, it’s crucial to inspect the screen enclosure for any damage, as high winds and flying debris can cause significant harm.
  • Pest issues: If you notice signs of pest infiltration, such as holes or gnaw marks on the screen, address the issue promptly and consider rescreening if the damage is extensive.
  • Aesthetic considerations: You might want to rescreen if the enclosure’s appearance has deteriorated significantly, affecting the overall aesthetics of your pool and property.
  • Fading or discoloration: If the screen material has faded or discolored, it’s a good time to consider rescreening for both aesthetic and functional reasons.

Timely rescreening will help maintain the integrity of your pool enclosure, ensuring that it continues to provide protection from insects, debris, and other elements while enhancing the visual appeal of your outdoor space.

Should I only replace the worn panels?

Replacing only the worn pool screen panels may seem like a cost-effective solution in the short term, but it’s essential to consider the overall condition of your pool screen enclosure and your long-term goals. If the worn panels are isolated and the rest of the structure is in good shape, replacing them can be a reasonable option.

However, several factors should influence your decision:

  • Age of the enclosure: If your pool screen enclosure is old, replacing only the worn panels may not address underlying structural issues. In such cases, a full replacement might be more cost-effective in the long run.
  • Aesthetics: Mismatched panels can affect the appearance of your pool area. If aesthetics are important to you, replacing all panels for a uniform look is advisable.
  • Future maintenance: If the enclosure shows signs of wear and tear, investing in a full replacement may be more cost-effective to avoid ongoing repairs.

The decision should be based on your specific circumstances, budget, and long-term plans for your pool area. Consulting with a professional can help you make an informed choice.

Choose the appropriate screen

Selecting the right screen for your pool area is crucial to enhance both safety and aesthetics. Here are some considerations to help you make the right choice:

Material

Opt for screens made from durable and weather-resistant materials like aluminum, vinyl, or fiberglass. These materials can withstand the harsh poolside environment, including exposure to chlorine and UV rays, without deteriorating.

Mesh size

Choose a screen with a small mesh size to keep out insects and debris effectively. 

Privacy

If you value privacy, select screens with a tighter weave or patterns that obstruct the view from the outside. This not only provides seclusion but also adds an element of elegance to your pool area.

Wind resistance

Consider the prevailing wind conditions in your area. Opt for screens designed to withstand strong winds to prevent them from tearing or becoming damaged.

Maintenance

Look for screens that are easy to clean and maintain. Regular maintenance will prolong the screen’s lifespan and keep it looking pristine.

Installation

Factor in the installation process. Some screens require professional installation, while others are more DIY-friendly. Make sure you choose one that aligns with your skill level and budget.

Local regulations

Check with your local authorities regarding any regulations or codes that might govern pool screens in your area. Compliance is essential to avoid legal issues.

Budget

Consider your budget. Quality pool screens come in a range of prices, so balance your needs with what you can afford.

Get enough bug protection

Small insects will disrupt anyone’s poolside experience. The enclosure screen must provide complete insect protection. Request a no-see-um screen. The thick Phifer mesh will keep most pests outside of the pool enclosure and away from any pool users.

Reinstall the enclosure fasteners

If you’re rescreening, consider replacing the enclosure fasteners as well. Cheaper fasteners are composed of metal and can corrode after a few years, costing more to replace than rescreening the enclosure. Combining the two procedures can greatly reduce repair expenses. Newer fasteners are constructed of more robust materials and will keep the screen in place even in high gusts.
